chapter: Fellow musicians: Kirk, Bunk, Parker, McShann
title: The Charlie Parker Foundation and a Kansas City jazz alternative
summary: Goodwin describes the foundation's lessons and housing with streets named for stars; Smith suggests honoring Kansas City jazz instead.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: (Whereupon, a brief recess was taken.)
Now, I'd like to ask you, Baby, and you Crook about the Charlie Parker Foundation, what it is set up to do and what you think the future will be. What do you think, Baby?
I think it will be a great thing.
What is it?
It's something -- it's supposed to be a statue, isn't it?
Well, it's a foundation.
Yeah, but they're supposed to build a statue.
Crook, you answer now.
Yeah, the Charlie Parker Foundation is a thing to glorify Charlie Parker.
Not Kansas City jazz?
Well --
Or Only incidentally.
Kansas City jazz would be secondary. This is strictly for Charlie Parker. It's the Charlie Parker Foundation.
Memorial.

Yes, but it's more or less a thing for young people. They have set up a standard where they teach young kids to play instruments. They have teachers that are hired and I think they have a government grant to operate it.
Now, they also have built -- have built a number of homes in these, you know, these two dwelling homes or whatever they call them, they're like duplexes. They're up --
Low income housing?
Yeah, low income housing. They instituted this through government funds and through raising money and they had a big thing here some years back where

Ella Fitzgerald, Mary Lou Williams and quite a few of the greats were here and at this particular housing project they have streets named after Mary Lou Williams, Ella Fitzgerald and several of the big names that did come and offer their services.
Yeah, Basie came in for that too, I believe?

Basie. See they named these streets in this project after these people and it's a wonderful thing, I can say, but I don't know too much about the financial part of the Charlie Parker Foundation at present because I don't know how long their grant from the government will last and I don't know -- I heard the other day that they are moving. I think they're moving out to Multipurpose Center out on Linwood, and I do hope that they continue.

Well, you know, it seems to me, gentlemen, that so many other Kansas City musicians did so much more for Kansas City music than Charlie Parker did and I can see a foundation for Kansas City jazz as such and with the names of all the great people that are still with us and so many that have passed being immortalized in a foundation. That's just my viewpoint. What do you think of that, Crook?
Well, I do think -- I think you have a great point there. I think in these terms. There are so many great musicians that come up around Kansas City as did
Charlie Parker and Ben Webster. Ben Webster was born --
Oh, we can go on and on and on.
We can go on and on naming quite a few musicians.
